scenario.title: The replacement camera is visible but cannot connect

model_calls.label: replay of a HAND-AUTHORED fixture (not model output)

simulation.boundary: Simulated station. Telemetry comes from LineSight's causal simulator with seeded faults; interventions change simulator state only. The transport model is a deliberately small burst-contention model and does not reproduce all GigE Vision behaviour or prove real hardware performance.
transport_assumptions: Each camera link and the host uplink are 1000 Mb/s full duplex.
Per-packet overhead on the wire: 20 B IP + 8 B UDP + 8 B GVSP header inside the packet, plus 14 B Ethernet header + 4 B FCS + 8 B preamble + 12 B inter-frame gap outside it.
A camera's throughput limit is enforced by an inter-packet delay; the camera then sends at a constant rate for the whole frame.
All cameras share one switch egress port toward the host with a fixed buffer; overflow bytes are dropped.
The host requests resends after a packet timeout. Each resend round costs the timeout plus the time to retransmit the missing bytes; a round recovers a fixed share of what is missing.
A frame is usable only if it completes and the inspection result reaches the PLC before the reject-gate deadline. The deadline is the gate travel time minus actuator margin.
Trigger-to-transmit start jitter per camera is uniform in +/- jitter_ms.

Other ports share the switch packet memory: at each burst a random share of the egress buffer (uniform 0..background_occupancy_max) is already occupied. This is a confounder that makes loss intermittent; it is a stand-in, not a measured property of any switch.
Average bandwidth is reported separately from burst behaviour: a link can be well under capacity on average and still overflow during synchronous bursts.

The transport model is a deliberately small burst-contention model and does not reproduce all GigE Vision behaviour or prove real hardware performance.
transport_assumptions: Each camera link and the host uplink are 1000 Mb/s full duplex.
Per-packet overhead on the wire: 20 B IP + 8 B UDP + 8 B GVSP header inside the packet, plus 14 B Ethernet header + 4 B FCS + 8 B preamble + 12 B inter-frame gap outside it.
A camera's throughput limit is enforced by an inter-packet delay; the camera then sends at a constant rate for the whole frame.
All cameras share one switch egress port toward the host with a fixed buffer; overflow bytes are dropped.
The host requests resends after a packet timeout. Each resend round costs the timeout plus the time to retransmit the missing bytes; a round recovers a fixed share of what is missing.
A frame is usable only if it completes and the inspection result reaches the PLC before the reject-gate deadline. The deadline is the gate travel time minus actuator margin.
Trigger-to-transmit start jitter per camera is uniform in +/- jitter_ms.

Other ports share the switch packet memory: at each burst a random share of the egress buffer (uniform 0..background_occupancy_max) is already occupied. This is a confounder that makes loss intermittent; it is a stand-in, not a measured property of any switch.
Average bandwidth is reported separately from burst behaviour: a link can be well under capacity on average and still overflow during synchronous bursts.

simulation.boundary: Simulated station. Telemetry comes from LineSight's causal simulator with seeded faults; interventions change simulator state only. The transport model is a deliberately small burst-contention model and does not reproduce all GigE Vision behaviour or prove real hardware performance.
transport_assumptions: Each camera link and the host uplink are 1000 Mb/s full duplex.
Per-packet overhead on the wire: 20 B IP + 8 B UDP + 8 B GVSP header inside the packet, plus 14 B Ethernet header + 4 B FCS + 8 B preamble + 12 B inter-frame gap outside it.
A camera's throughput limit is enforced by an inter-packet delay; the camera then sends at a constant rate for the whole frame.
All cameras share one switch egress port toward the host with a fixed buffer; overflow bytes are dropped.
The host requests resends after a packet timeout. Each resend round costs the timeout plus the time to retransmit the missing bytes; a round recovers a fixed share of what is missing.
A frame is usable only if it completes and the inspection result reaches the PLC before the reject-gate deadline. The deadline is the gate travel time minus actuator margin.
Trigger-to-transmit start jitter per camera is uniform in +/- jitter_ms.

Other ports share the switch packet memory: at each burst a random share of the egress buffer (uniform 0..background_occupancy_max) is already occupied. This is a confounder that makes loss intermittent; it is a stand-in, not a measured property of any switch.
Average bandwidth is reported separately from burst behaviour: a link can be well under capacity on average and still overflow during synchronous bursts.
